centerpiece.reader_produces: The reader drags the five pillar-weight sliders (Reputation / Citations / Teaching / International / Output) or taps a preset chip; all 218 universities re-rank live and a different school becomes world #1. Moving between presets alone manufactures Oxford, MIT or Michigan as #1 from the SAME data — the reader produces the thesis 'best is a slider position, not a fact' with their own hands, BEFORE the prose names any champion.
controls: Five labelled range sliders — Reputation (rep), Citations (cite), Teaching (teach), International (intl), Output (vol) — integer 0-10, seeded at the BALANCED preset (all equal) so the untouched widget reproduces the published #1 Oxford 87.02.
Five preset chips as native <button>: Balanced / QS-like / THE-like / ARWU-like / Output-only, placed ABOVE the sliders (each chip sets all five slider values then recomputes).

client_model.inputs: (weights, topN)  where weights = {rep,cite,teach,intl,vol} (non-negative numbers; the fn normalises by the weight sum), topN optional int
client_model.returns: [{rank, name, country, score}] sorted best-first (218 rows); pass topN=15 for the leaderboard
client_model.presets_source: REWEIGHT_PRESETS in the same file (balanced 1,1,1,1,1 / qs_like 5,2,2,1,0 / the_like 3,3,3,1,0 / arwu_like 0,3,0,0,4 / output_only 0,0,0,0,1) — inline these, do NOT re-tune
client_model.cost: closed-form O(n log n), <1ms; recompute on every slider input (no debounce needed, but a --dur-xs crossfade keeps it flicker-free)

centerpiece.at_rest: Sliders at BALANCED. Leaderboard shows reweightRankings(balanced, 15): #1 University of Oxford, then Harvard 86.22, Cambridge 83.64, Michigan 82.84, Stanford 82.66. A big '#1' champion card reads 'University of Oxford'. The live blended score of the current #1 is exposed as a BARE parseable number: 87.02 (with a separate static unit node, e.g. 'blended score', OUTSIDE the parsed span).
centerpiece.on_interact: On any slider input OR preset-chip click: FIRST `if (vOn()) return;` (Verify coexistence) — then read the five slider values -> call reweightRankings({rep,cite,teach,intl,vol}, 15) -> re-sort/re-join the leaderboard bars to their new positions with a short crossfade (D3 join + transition, motion.json --dur-xs on high-frequency drag) -> update the champion card's NAME + score -> write the new #1's bare score into [data-play-out=int_01]. When the CHAMPION actually changes (name differs from the previous render), the crown badge does a single gentle pop (motion.json --ease-spring, once) — not on every drag.
centerpiece.payoff: The five presets crown THREE different schools from the identical 218-university data: Balanced -> Oxford (87.02), QS-like -> MIT (96.25), Output-only -> Michigan (100.0) [THE-like -> MIT 95.16; ARWU-like -> Michigan 95.24]. A running line ('You just crowned ___') makes the reader realise they manufactured a world #1 by moving sliders. This lands BEFORE the [ana_12] paragraph that names Oxford / MIT / Michigan.
centerpiece.placement: PLAY-FIRST, at/before the reveal in edt_06. Number count-up (motion.json --dur-count) on the #1 score when a preset chip is tapped (skip the count-up on continuous drag).

verify_coexistence._note: MANDATORY for every element above so the built controls COEXIST with the Inspector/Verify layer (E1 verify-coexistence + the shared playbook verify_coexistence). This is what the Playtester's verify_coexist check enforces.
verify_coexistence.rule_1_vOn_guard: Define once near the top of the script: `const vOn = () => document.documentElement.classList.contains('verify-on');`. The FIRST line of EVERY feature handler (slider input, button/chip click, <select> change, tile pick, Reveal, keydown Enter/Space, and any hover/focus side-effect) early-returns: `if (vOn()) return;`. Guard the MUTATING handlers only — never guard the initial render()/baseline draw (the at-rest published numbers must still paint).
verify_coexistence.rule_2_never_stopPropagation: No feature handler calls stopPropagation() (nor a preventDefault that swallows the bubble). Under verify-on the gesture must be free to bubble to the provenance container so the Verify engine's delegated handler opens the drawer.
verify_coexistence.rule_3_role_link_only_for_non_control_su: Native controls (<input>, <button>, <select>) are IN the Verify INNER_INTERACTIVE allow-list, so the engine defers to them and the vOn() guard alone makes them inert under Verify — use native controls for ALL the sliders/chips/tiles/selects above (best for a11y). The role=link trick is needed ONLY when a NON-control clickable sub-target sits OVER a provenance-bearing container (e.g. a clickable leaderboard row or a clickable chart region layered on the data-des chart): make that sub-target `role="link" tabindex="0"` (OUT of the allow-list) + vOn()-guarded + never stopPropagation, so under Verify its click bubbles to the container's provenance hit. Do NOT give such sub-targets their own data-* provenance id (that would split one claim into many hits).
verify_coexistence.provenance_keying: Provenance stays on the CHART/READOUT container (its data-des id), ONE per element. The interactive recompute is NOT itself a separate provenance claim; the data-play-out readout node is a NON-provenance hook (in no validate tuple/schema) the Playtester reads.

scrollytelling_note: The spine is a sequence of discrete evidence beats, not one morphing sticky graphic, so no scrollytelling rig. The mandatory full-bleed scroll BACKGROUND (night-campus cinematic) is the Cinematographer's stage (des_ / sct_ imagery), separate from these playgrounds.

int_02 result grid: fade/rise in on Reveal (--dur-md, --ease-out).
int_03 top-10 rows: D3 position transition on lens toggle (--dur-md); crown slides to the new #1.

int_07 dumbbell + 'you are here' marker: marker fades/rings in on lookup (--dur-md).
All: animate transform/opacity only; honor prefers-reduced-motion (motion.json collapses tokens — bars/positions appear at final state, no motion).
